name: Goldman Sachs
description: Goldman Sachs is an investment bank and bank holding company with two big businesses and a shrinking third. Global Banking & Markets (71 percent of 2025 net revenues) earns advisory and underwriting fees, and makes markets (buys and sells for clients and sometimes takes the other side) in bonds, currencies, commodities and equities, plus financing to trading clients such as prime brokerage and structured lending. Asset & Wealth Management (29 percent) collects annual fees on assets it supervises ($3.6 trillion at year-end 2025), incentive fees, and interest on private-bank lending, and books gains or losses on its own investments. Platform Solutions, mostly the Apple Card credit card program, is being wound down: Goldman agreed in December 2025 to move the program to another issuer over about 24 months, and sold the GM card program in 2025. Results swing with deal activity and trading volumes; 2025 pre-tax earnings were $21.9 billion on net revenues of $58.3 billion.

businessLines.name: Global Banking & Markets
businessLines.how: Corporations, governments and institutional investors pay fees for advising on mergers and for underwriting stock and bond sales (paid per deal, when it closes); they also trade through Goldman, which earns the bid-offer spread and gains on positions it holds while making markets, commissions on executing and clearing trades, and net interest on financing it provides to clients (prime brokerage margin loans, repo, structured lending).
businessLines.description: Investment banking (advisory, equity and debt underwriting), FICC (fixed income, currencies, commodities) intermediation and financing, Equities intermediation and financing, and Other (relationship lending and acquisition financing, transaction banking, investing activities). Since Q4 2025 it also includes transaction banking, moved from Platform Solutions.

operatingProfit.note: Pre-tax earnings; FY2024 $14,529M; pre-tax margin 42.4% computed. Segment return on average common equity 16.4% (13.8% in 2024).

businessLines.name: Asset & Wealth Management
businessLines.how: Institutions and individuals pay annual asset-based fees on assets Goldman supervises, plus incentive fees when funds beat return hurdles; wealth clients borrow and deposit, so the bank earns net interest; and Goldman books gains or losses on its own investments in companies, real estate and infrastructure.
businessLines.description: Manages client assets across equity, fixed income and alternatives (hedge funds, credit, private equity, real estate); wealth advisory for ultra-high-net-worth clients, private banking and lending, Marcus deposits; and investments the firm makes alongside clients. Historical principal investments are being sold and replaced with a third-party-funds-driven model.

operatingProfit.note: Pre-tax earnings; FY2024 $4,865M (-15%); pre-tax margin 24.7% computed; return on average common equity 12.5% (14.6% in 2024).

businessLines.name: Platform Solutions
businessLines.how: Card customers pay interest and fees on balances; Goldman is the issuer and funds the loans with deposits, so revenue is net interest income less partnership costs and credit losses, and it is being run off.
businessLines.description: Substantially all revenue is Apple Card (credit cards issued in partnership with Apple, plus deposits raised from Apple Card customers) and exited businesses such as the General Motors card program (sold in 2025). In December 2025 Goldman agreed to transition Apple Card to another issuer over about 24 months; the loan portfolio moved to held for sale in December 2025.

revenue.note: Net revenues; FY2024 $2,129M; FY2023 $2,058M. 2025 includes a $1,380M benefit (negative provision) in the provision for credit losses and total operating expenses of $1,380M (10-K segment table).
